content.title: About
content.content: Beef dinner is a ready‑to‑eat frozen meal featuring premium beef, vegetables and sauce, produced by NFS. The portion is flash‑frozen to lock in flavor and nutrients, and is intended for quick reheating in a microwave or on the stovetop.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The product is manufactured at NFS facilities, known for their expertise in frozen foods.
Flash‑freezing technology retains up to 90 % of vitamins and minerals.
Each serving is sized for one adult (approximately 350 g of finished product).
Only natural ingredients are used; no artificial colourings are added.
Packaging is made from recyclable plastic suitable for secondary processing.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: The heme iron in beef supports normal blood formation and oxygen transport.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meal supplies B12, B6 and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low carbohydrate content
items.content: Suitable for low‑carb diets as the main energy sources are protein and fat.

items.title: Zinc source
items.content: Zinc from beef helps maintain immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The meal contains a moderate amount of salt; people monitoring sodium intake should account for it.

items.title: Complete thawing required
items.content: Insufficiently thawed meals may heat unevenly, increasing the risk of foodborne illness.

items.title: Not suitable for vegetarians or vegans
items.content: Contains beef, therefore not appropriate for plant‑based diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thaw the portion in the refrigerator for 4–6 hours or use the microwave’s defrost function. Then heat in the microwave on high for 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway through. For stovetop preparation, place the contents in a saucepan, add 2 ml of water and heat over medium heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring regularly.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen meal at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, consume within 2 hours and do not store in the refrigerator for more than 24 hours.

chicken-or-turkey-and-noodles-with-gravy.title: Chicken or turkey and noodles with gravy

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of boiled chicken or turkey served with noodles and a thick gravy. The meat is steamed or boiled, then sliced, while the noodles are made from wheat flour. The gravy is usually prepared from broth, flour and spices, giving the meal a rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are among the most widely consumed white meats worldwide.
Egg or wheat noodles are common in traditional dishes across many cultures.
A broth‑based gravy increases the bioavailability of nutrients from the meat.
The dish is often served in school cafeterias because it is easy to digest and protein‑rich.
In some regions vegetables (carrots, peas) are added to boost nutritional value.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat (especially turkey)
items.content: White meat contains less saturated fat than red meat, which is heart‑friendly.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat is abundant in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals – iron and zinc
items.content: Iron from poultry is highly absorbable, and zinc is important for immune health.

items.title: Carbohydrates from noodles provide energy
items.content: Wheat noodles supply a quick source of glucose needed for physical activity.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken or turkey proteins.

items.title: Sodium content in gravy
items.content: Prepared gravies often contain salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor salmonella or campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Gluten in noodles
items.content: Traditional wheat noodles contain gluten, making the dish unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, mixing chicken or turkey pieces with noodles and drizzling the gravy over them. Garnish with fresh herbs (parsley, dill) or lightly sautéed vegetables for added flavor and color.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftovers within 2 hours of cooking, place them in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat thoroughly to a rolling boil to destroy any possible bacteria.

content.title: About
content.content: Vanilla wafer is a crisp cookie with a delicate vanilla aroma. It is made from a thin dough to which vanilla extract is added, then baked until golden. The wafer works as a standalone snack or as an accompaniment to tea or coffee.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vanilla flavor is obtained from natural vanilla beans or their extract.
Thin layers of dough give the wafer a light, crunchy texture, distinguishing it from denser cookies.
Traditionally popular in Europe, especially in Scandinavian countries and Germany.
Vanilla wafers are often used in dessert compositions as a base for cakes, mousses and ice cream.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Vanilla wafers usually contain a small amount of fat, making them a lighter snack compared with butter-rich cookies.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The dough provides a quick source of energy through simple carbohydrates.

items.title: Vanilla antioxidants
items.content: Vanilla contains antioxidants such as vanillin, which may have mild anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional wafers are made from wheat flour and may be unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Vanilla wafers are often sweetened, so individuals monitoring blood sugar should watch portion size.

items.title: Flavorings
items.content: Some manufacturers use artificial flavorings instead of natural vanilla, which can trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The cookie can be enjoyed on its own, broken into pieces and added to ice cream, yogurt or fruit salad. It is also used as a base layer in desserts and cakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the wafer in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage keep it in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent moisture absorption.

content.title: About
content.content: The flavored rice and pasta mixture is a ready‑to‑cook blend that combines selected rice, small pasta shapes, and a blend of herbs and spices. It is designed for quick preparation of a tasty side dish suitable for both meat and vegetarian meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The mix unites two popular staples—rice and pasta—offering a convenient solution for varied menus.
Typical seasonings include dried basil, oregano, garlic and paprika, giving the dish a Mediterranean aroma.
No pre‑soaking of the rice is required, saving preparation time.
The product is widely used in cafeterias and catering because of its fast cooking and consistent flavor.
Some versions contain small pieces of dried vegetables that enhance the flavor profile.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice and pasta provide sustained energy by slowly releasing glucose.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: Durum‑wheat pasta adds a modest amount of plant‑based protein to the diet.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Herbs and whole‑grain pasta supply vitamins B1, B3 and B6, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The mixture is virtually fat‑free, making it suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain pasta and added dried vegetables increase fiber content, aiding digestion.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The pasta component contains gluten, so the product is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some blends may have a higher salt level; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Flavorings may include food colorings and taste enhancers that some consumers prefer to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour 250 ml of boiling water over the mixture, cover, and let stand for 10–12 minutes, then fluff with a fork. Optionally add vegetables, meat or seafood for a more substantial meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package. After opening, use within 3–4 weeks and keep moisture out.

content.title: About
content.content: Hash, NS is a ready‑to‑eat product made from finely chopped beef, seasoned with spices and a modest amount of fat. It is designed for quick preparation of stews, soups, and stir‑fries. The product has a uniform texture, heats quickly, and retains a characteristic meaty flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Hash is often used in military rations because of its long shelf life.
The production process includes thermal treatment and vacuum packaging, preserving aroma and nutrients.
It can serve as a base for dishes without additional meat chopping.
Hash, NS is commonly included in ready‑meal kits for hikers and expeditions.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: A serving provides about 20 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef is rich in heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Hash fits well into low‑carb dietary plans.

items.title: Convenient storage
items.content: Sealed in airtight packaging, it remains stable for up to 12 months.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to beef may experience reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The product contains added salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Thermal handling
items.content: When reheating, ensure the internal temperature reaches at least 75 °C to prevent bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hash, NS can be heated in a skillet, microwave, or added to soups. For oven preparation, bake at 180 °C for 10–12 minutes. It pairs well with vegetables, potatoes, or grains.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated at +4 °C and consume within 3–5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Canned potato (NS) is boiled potatoes packed in airtight cans with added salt and sometimes spices. The product retains a soft texture and characteristic flavor, suitable for quick meal preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning allows potatoes to be stored for 2‑3 years without loss of taste.
Cans usually contain low‑starch potato varieties to keep the pieces intact during heat treatment.
NS stands for “not salty”, meaning the product has a moderate salt level.
Canned potatoes are often used in military rations and backpacking meals.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B6, which supports protein metabolism and nerve function.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Helps maintain fluid‑electrolyte balance and normal blood pressure.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: A modest amount of dietary fiber aids digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Canned potatoes contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Even with the NS label, some salt is present; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Bisphenol A
items.content: Older cans may be lined with BPA‑containing coating; choose products in modern packaging.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: If a can is damaged, bacterial growth is possible, so always check the integrity of the packaging.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned potatoes can be eaten cold in salads, heated in the microwave, added to soups, stews, or mashed. After opening, drain the brine and optionally season with fresh herbs or spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, transfer the contents to an airtight container and keep refrigerated, using within 2‑3 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Iced brewed green tea unsweetened is a refreshing beverage made from Camellia sinensis leaves that undergo a cold‑water extraction. It retains the light, vegetal aroma of green tea while being served chilled and without any added sweeteners.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green tea is rich in polyphenols, especially catechins, which have strong antioxidant properties.
Cold brewing preserves more vitamin C than hot brewing because the lower temperature does not degrade it.
In Japan, cold green tea (mucha) is traditionally served during summer to cool the body.
Without sugar, the drink is very low in calories – about 0‑2 kcal per 100 ml.
Leaves used for cold brew are often younger, giving the tea a milder flavor.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Catechins help neutralize free radicals, supporting cellular health.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Regular consumption of green tea may help lower LDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: Metabolism boost
items.content: Caffeine and L‑theanine can increase metabolic rate and aid fat oxidation.

items.title: Sugar‑free hydration
items.content: Provides fluid without added calories, making it ideal for hydration.

items.title: Cognitive enhancement
items.content: The combination of caffeine and L‑theanine improves focus and alertness.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience jitteriness, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Green tea can amplify the effects of anticoagulants and certain antidepressants.

items.title: Iron absorption
items.content: Tannins may reduce iron absorption, so people with anemia should drink tea between meals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the iced unsweetened green tea on its own, or add a slice of lemon, mint, or ginger for extra flavor. It works well in cocktails, smoothies, or as a base for marinades.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared beverage in a sealed bottle in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Flavor may diminish with prolonged storage.

content.title: About
content.content: Veal Parmigiana is a baked veal cutlet layered with tomato sauce and melted mozzarella and Parmesan cheese. The dish originates from Italian cuisine, where “parmigiana” denotes a cheese‑topped bake. Veal makes the dish tender, while the sauce adds a bright tomato flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional parmigiana is made with chicken or eggplant; veal is considered a more luxurious variant.
It is often served with pasta or polenta and garnished with fresh basil.
Parmesan used in the recipe should be aged at least 12 months for optimal flavor.
Veal cutlets are usually pounded to about 5 mm thickness to ensure even cooking.
The original Neapolitan version used only tomato sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan, without extra herbs.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Veal provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat, including veal, is a good source of heme iron, which helps prevent anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Veal is rich in vitamin B12 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Mozzarella and Parmesan add calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Lycopene in tomato sauce
items.content: Tomatoes provide lycopene, an antioxidant that may reduce the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Cheese and meat can increase saturated fat intake, so the dish should be enjoyed in moderation.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Tomato sauce and cheeses are often salty; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Veal must be cooked through to avoid salmonella or Campylobacter contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve veal parmigiana hot, typically with a side of pasta, mashed potatoes or fresh vegetables. Sprinkle with fresh basil or oregano for extra aroma. The dish can be cut into portions and eaten with a fork and knife.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in the oven or microwave to retain the cheese’s crispy crust.
